concepts.def: Extension of a spring is proportional to force.
Point where spring stops returning to shape.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Hang a weight on a spring - it stretches. Double the weight, double the stretch.

This is Hooke's Law: extension is proportional to force, up to the elastic limit.

Past the elastic limit, the spring stays stretched and won't bounce back.

Drop a skydiver. Gravity pulls down, air resistance pushes up.

At first, gravity wins - they accelerate. As they get faster, air resistance grows.

Eventually forces balance. They fall at a constant terminal velocity.

Opening a parachute increases air resistance, forces unbalance, they slow down to a new safe terminal velocity.

A free-body diagram shows all forces on one object as arrows.

Arrow length = size of force. Arrow direction = direction of force.

For a swimming fish: weight down, upthrust up, thrust forward, drag back. If they all balance, the fish swims at constant speed.
